title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, generated by loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. The symmetric group S_3 acts on it as outer automorphisms, generated by σ_∞ (the involution swapping 0 and 1) and ρ (the 3-cycle 0→1→∞). This sheet is numbered 317 in the 'Deuxième partie' sequel to the Longue Marche.

Grothendieck redoes computations from an earlier text [C]. The object is an outer automorphism u of π̂_{0,3} that commutes with S_3 and sends each inertia class to its ρ-th power, for some ρ∈Ẑ*. Careful: the letter ρ denotes both this cyclotomic-type exponent and the 3-cycle automorphism.

Step 1: normalisation. He claims such an outer action lifts uniquely to an actual automorphism that commutes with σ_∞ and commutes with ρ up to inner automorphisms. Uniqueness relies on the fixed subgroup π̂_{0,3}^{σ_∞} being trivial, as the margin note says.

Step 2: parametrisation. These lifts correspond bijectively to pairs (g_0, ρ), with g_0 ∈ π̂_{0,3} mod L_0 (the closed subgroup generated by l_0) and ρ ∈ Ẑ*. The next page (11) gives the formulas: u(l_0) = g_0 l_0^ρ g_0^{-1} and u(l_1) = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^ρ σ_∞(g_0)^{-1}. He sets h_0 = σ_∞(g_0)^{-1} g_0 = [σ_∞, g_0^{-1}]. Then h_0 is the comparison element between the conjugators of l_1 and l_0, i.e. Drinfeld's f(x,y) up to convention. The form σ(g)^{-1}g automatically gives σ_∞(h_0)h_0 = 1. This is Drinfeld's 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1, built in here by writing f as a 'coboundary' for the Z/2-action.

Step 3: conditions. The pair must satisfy three conditions:
- (9) the images still satisfy the product-one relation: l_1^ρ · int(h_0)(l_0^ρ) · int(l_1^γ ρ(h_0)^{-1})(l_∞^ρ) = 1.
- (10) h_0 l_0^{-γ} ρ^{-1}(h_0) = l_1^γ ρ(h_0)^{-1} l_∞^γ.
- (10 bis), the condition that u commute with the 3-cycle: (l_0^γ h_0^{-1})·ρ(l_0^γ h_0^{-1})·ρ^2(l_0^γ h_0^{-1}) = 1.
Here γ∈Ẑ is determined by u, and the margin says γ = (ρ−1)/2. Thus (10 bis) is exactly Drinfeld's hexagon/3-cycle relation (II): f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m f(x,y)x^m = 1 with m = (λ−1)/2. Together these define the 'S_3 part' of GT̂, i.e. the conditions on (λ,f) coming from M_{0,3} with its S_3 symmetry, without the pentagon.

Step 4: purpose. The next page transports u to the group Ĝ^+_{0,3} generated by σ_∞ (order 2) and ρ (order 3). This is a profinite Z/2*Z/3, i.e. profinite PSL_2(Z), the orbifold fundamental group of the j-line (P^1−{0,1,∞})/S_3. The previous page identifies it with π̂_{0,3}/⟨⟨l_1^2, l_∞^3⟩⟩. He derives u(σ_∞) = σ_∞ and u(ρ) = gρ with g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^γ ρ(g_0)^{-1}.

The overall aim is to find the conditions on Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q), and on its candidate 'Teichmüller' substitute, imposed by the S_3-equivariant orbifold structure. The previous page anticipates 'toute une kyrielle de conditions de même nature sur Γ'.
errors: Notational overload: ρ denotes both the exponent in Ẑ* and the order-3 automorphism, so (10 bis) and the margin 'γ=(ρ−1)/2' must be read with care. Also (ρ−1)/2 makes sense in Ẑ only since ρ is a unit, hence odd at 2. Not a real error.

(9) is written with l_1^{ρ'} and the margin suggests ρ'=ρ, so there is some unsettled bookkeeping. Grothendieck himself notes on the next page that 'en toute rigueur' one must also require that u(l_0), u(l_1) topologically generate π̂_{0,3}. So the bijection claimed on this page is incomplete as stated: a surjectivity/automorphy condition is missing.
The relation between (9), (10) and (10 bis) is not clarified; the margin suggests one of them is superfluous. As written, the system is redundant rather than wrong.

Uniqueness of the normalised lift needs π̂_{0,3}^{σ_∞} = 1. He only 'admits' this in the margin. It is true: discretely, by a first-letter argument for the swap x↔y, and also for the profinite free group.

ideas.what: Parametrising S_3-commuting outer automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} with cyclotomic exponent by pairs (g_0, ρ), with f = h_0 = σ_∞(g_0)^{-1}g_0
ideas.modern_name: elements (λ,f) of Drinfeld's GT̂ (the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x)=1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990; Ihara 1991 for the profinite version
ideas.where_published: Spirit announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); explicit formulas not in published texts as far as I know

ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld's hexagon relation (II) in GT̂, with m=(λ−1)/2

ideas.what: Normalising outer actions to genuine automorphisms commuting with σ_∞, using triviality of π̂^{σ_∞}
ideas.modern_name: choice of tangential-basepoint / symmetric lift; fixed points of an involution of a free profinite group

ideas.what: Transporting the action to the order-2/order-3 orbifold group Ĝ^+_{0,3} ≅ (Z/2*Z/3)^ (j-line), with u(σ)=σ, u(ρ)=gρ
ideas.modern_name: action of GT̂ on profinite PSL_2(Z) / π_1^{orb} of M_{1,1}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions M_{1,1} and the 'jeu de Lego' but not these formulas

missed.claim: An explicit pre-Drinfeld derivation (early 1980s) of the two 'S_3' defining relations of GT̂ from outer actions on π̂_{0,3} commuting with S_3. It includes the half-integer m=(λ−1)/2 and the cocycle form f = σ(g)^{-1}g that makes relation (I) automatic.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck's anticipation of GT is folklore, but the exact formulas and their derivation are rarely cited. The g_0 parametrisation, writing f as a Z/2-coboundary, is a slightly different presentation from Drinfeld's.

missed.claim: Directly linking the S_3-conditions on Γ to an action on the j-line orbifold group (Z/2*Z/3)^ = π̂_{0,3}/⟨⟨l_1², l_∞³⟩⟩, presented as the 'Teichmüller' extension M_{0,3} of Γ.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This matches later work on GT acting on profinite PSL_2(Z) (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura). It is of mainly historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, explicit early derivation of Drinfeld's relations (I) and (II), predating Drinfeld. However, it is broadly known that the Longue Marche and its sequels contain such S_3 computations, and the results are now standard. Its value is mainly historical and in its normalisation details.
